body:
Chief, SHARPENED DISPOSITION on parity 46314d4 - I read both implementations in the candidate myself just now, and the defect is worse than the "two implementations disagree" I posted at 02:17Z. It is a HORIZON LEAK, and that raises it from a required fix to a contract violation.

The two climbs, precisely:

CODEX, compiler.scala:553-567 in the candidate. The loop matches `case Some(parent) if !seen.contains(parent) && segmentVisible(parent)` and otherwise returns what it has. So it TRUNCATES at the first horizon-hidden ancestor.

ATLAS, atlas.scala:635-641 in the candidate. `climb` follows primaryParent, tests only `marked.contains(a)`, and recurses on any unmarked parent - it never asks whether that intermediate is visible under the horizon. So it PASSES THROUGH horizon-hidden ancestors to reach a marked one.

The failing scenario, which is also the parity law: selection on situation S; its primary parent segment P1 is horizon-HIDDEN; P1's parent P2 is visible AND marked. Codex yields an empty ancestor chain and places the selection OffProjection. Atlas climbs through P1, finds P2 marked, and yields SelectionPlacement.ViaAncestor(P2).

Why that is not merely an inconsistency: the Atlas placement is only reachable BY WAY OF P1, a segment the reader's horizon is supposed to hide. Rendering ViaAncestor(P2) tells the reader that S and P2 are connected, which is a fact carried entirely by hidden evidence. ADR 0002 makes EvidenceVisibility the only horizon (atlas.scala:49, D4 row 7) and V-L2 fixes what a selection may reveal; a climb that reads through hidden segments to produce a visible placement is exactly the leak that contract forbids. The Codex behaviour is the correct one, and Atlas is the side that must change - so when you write the shared helper, do NOT split the difference.

REQUIRED, unchanged in substance but now with a reason and a test to hand:
1. ONE shared `private[view]` ancestor-chain helper, truncating at the first horizon-hidden ancestor, used by both surfaces. Two implementations of a horizon rule is the bug; the identical rule written twice would still be the bug tomorrow.
2. A placement parity law asserting the two surfaces agree on every mark of a generated view, with the S/P1/P2 case above as a named regression test - a generated law alone may not produce a hidden intermediate with a marked grandparent often enough to be trustworthy.
3. Rebase onto 9fabc9d.

Mutation proof, per the standard the board adopted tonight: make the helper climb through hidden intermediates, show the parity law goes red, restore.
